top_problem: The page is a web hero banner stacked on a plain list. The adobe-to-grain-elevator fusion is a real idea on paper, but it does not read at arm's length: the plum sits on indigo with almost no value separation, so the headhouse disappears into the sky, the domed silos read as clouds or scallops, and the stepped crown reads as a generic Mesoamerican ziggurat. Below the horizon the art never touches the menu. Compare ref-02 panel 2, where the sun and stair crop the page edge and frame the list. The boldest missing idea is an art gesture that runs down the page edge beside the columns, so the cantina/Iowa horizon holds the menu instead of sitting above it like a letterhead.
remove: The three descending 'pointer' parapet steps. They are a second stepping motif beside the escalonado crown, they read as a stair or pyramid cliché, and they do not actually point at the cocktail axis (they land at x 430 against an axis at 408). Letting the silhouette start at the adobe block also quiets the amber band.
fixes: Equalise the margins: bring the bottom margin to 72 px (or the sides to 52) within ±1 mm, and move CANTINA and its sub-line from x 68 to the x 72 text edge. This lifts criterion 6 off the measured-failure cap of 40.

Make the silhouette legible: raise its value contrast against the indigo (for example a much lighter or warmer plum, or let the amber glow wrap up behind the tower), and redraw the elevator with a clearly readable gallery and bin cluster so the Iowa half passes the squint test instead of reading as an office block with clouds.

Pick one alignment system: set Cocktails flush left on the same 3-column grid (for example spanning columns 1-2, with the sub heads and names on x 72), or centre everything. The centred wedding-program block over flush-left columns makes the page read as two menus.

Carry the art into the reading area by cropping the plum wall or silo column down the right trim beside Draft Beer/Cider (with text kept in the safe inset), so word and image interlock as in ref-02 panels 1, 2 and 5 rather than meeting at a hard horizontal seam.

Give the flat vector a material voice the concept justifies (a subtle two-pass screen-print offset or a paper tooth on the field only, kept away from the text), and bring the Spirits and Wine columns to end on the same line as Cider (y 1004) so there is no 40 px ragged foot.

lens: content: items and prices against build/draft_doc.json, ingredient completeness (public_components), flow
top_problem: The design is only complete for cocktails. Every non-cocktail item is left with its taxonomy stub ('Blanco tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour', 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Hop-forward draft IPA'), and these either repeat the item name or name a class. Beer has no ABV, wine has no region, and spirits have no brand, age or pour size. These gaps appear only as 'open gaps' in proposal.md. Nothing on the menu or in the doc flags them as missing_ingredients. So 10 of 14 items fail criterion 8's standard, and the flat grey descriptions make the lower tier read as placeholder copy under a strong cocktail block.
problems: Items and prices: all 14 items match the draft exactly (Manhattan 15, Margarita 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Dry Cider 8). Nothing is invented, changed or dropped. The price format is consistent: whole numbers, no $, inline 1 em after the name.

Hidden component handled correctly: aromatic bitters are left out of the Manhattan (public_components aromatic-bitters=false). The Old Fashioned (house_recipe=false) shows ingredient names only, with no quantities.

Garnishes (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel, cocktail cherry) are cited to recipe_versions ids (f06abb74, 14d45e57, 7095fd3d) and the cherry comes from draft components. I did not re-query them; the accuracy reviewer should confirm.

Criterion 8: beer has no ABV, wine has no grape-plus-region line (Brut Rosé does not even name a grape), and spirits have no age statement, brand or pour size. 'Blanco tequila pour' and 'VSOP Cognac pour' restate the name. The menu carries no missing_ingredients flag.

Voice split (criterion 10): cocktails use middot ingredient lists, while everything else uses database-class phrases. The Margarita alone adds a tasting-note line, 'Bright and citrus-forward', so one cocktail is written differently from the other three.

Flow (criterion 5): the section order is Cocktails, Spirits, Wine, Draft Beer + Cider. The draft and the scorecard's reference order is cocktails, beer, wine, spirits. Beer is a core category at a Mexican cantina, yet here it lands last in the far-right column, under Spirits and Wine. Putting agave spirits second can be defended; demoting beer is not argued anywhere.

Structural inconsistency: Spirits and Wine keep italic sub heads (Agave, Brandy, By the Glass, Sparkling). Beer's only sub, 'Draft', is folded into the head 'Draft Beer', and Cider has no sub. So the three lower columns use three different heading systems. The right column also runs about 40 px longer than the other two.

Reading path: the centred cocktail block switches to a flush-left three-column tier, so the eye has to re-anchor. Centred, ragged ingredient lines of different widths (Margarita and Old Fashioned are wide, Manhattan is narrow) are harder to scan than a flush edge.

Prices (criterion 3): the inline muted price at 1 em after the name keeps pairing tight and passes association. But the price x position shifts on every row, there is no figure alignment within a column, and the price colour is the same grey as the descriptions, so prices do not read as a system.
Taglines and captions: only the sub-line '& cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' appears. It states no item fact, so it passes. There are no prop captions or side rails.
No non-alcoholic section. The draft has none either, so I am not failing the design for it. But a Mexican restaurant with no NA option is a menu gap the Coordinator should raise with the venue.
fixes: Flag missing_ingredients in the doc for every wine (grape and region, and producer if known), beer (ABV and brewery) and spirit (brand, age and pour size), and ask the venue for them. Until the answers come in, replace the name-repeating stubs with draft-only wording that does not restate the name (for example Cognac VSOP: 'Cognac, aged VSOP'). Do not invent anything to fill the gaps.
Reorder the lower tier to Draft Beer + Cider, then Wine, then Spirits, or argue the agave-first order in the proposal. Right now beer, a core cantina category, is buried last with no reason given.

Use one heading system across the lower tier: either restore 'Draft' as an italic sub under a 'Beer' head, or collapse the Spirits and Wine subs the same way. Then balance the column heights so the right column does not run long.
Give every cocktail the same description structure: either drop 'Bright and citrus-forward' from the Margarita or write a one-line, fact-only note for each cocktail from its recipe data.

Separate prices from the descriptions by colour or weight (for example a darker ink than the #5B5058 description grey). In the three flush-left columns, consider a tabular right-aligned price edge per column so the numbers read as one system.

lens: Checked that every printed ingredient, garnish and label traces to build/draft_doc.json and to phg.recipe_versions through menu_items.current_recipe_version_id (gateway log_id 214). Checked how descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png.
top_problem: Every fact checks out, but the words fail. All four garnishes match their recipe_versions rows: Margarita lime wheel (rv f06abb74), Manhattan cocktail cherry (rv 9fb77eaa), House Daiquiri lime coin (rv 14d45e57) and Brown Butter Old Fashioned orange peel (rv 7095fd3d). Every ingredient matches the draft components and the accents on Añejo and Rosé are correct. Aromatic bitters are correctly hidden on the Manhattan (public_components aromatic-bitters=false). All 14 prices match menu_items.menu_price. The problem is that about half the descriptions only repeat the item name or read like database categories: 'Blanco tequila pour', 'Añejo tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour', 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Dry sparkling cider', 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine'. That triggers the criterion 12 automatic fail. The cocktails are bare ingredient lists with no voice, except the Margarita, whose tasting note 'Bright and citrus-forward' drops onto its own centred line and reads like a separate item. Apart from the CANTINA wordmark, and the Añejo and blanco item names and Agave subhead that come straight from the draft, the menu has no Mexican voice and no Spanish kickers, and the lower tier could belong to any Iowa City pub. Also note that phg.menu_items has a 15th item, Junmai Ginjo at 12, which is not in draft_doc.json and is not printed. This is not a gate fail here because the draft is the declared source, but the Coordinator should confirm the draft is current.
fixes: Criterion 12: rewrite the spirits, wine, beer and cider lines in guest language from the draft facts only, without restating the name (for example Pinot Grigio 'crisp, dry white' rather than 'Dry white wine'), and ask the Coordinator for the missing producer, region, ABV and pour size (missing_ingredients) instead of printing category labels.

Criterion 14: move 'Bright and citrus-forward' to the front of the Margarita line, or give every cocktail a matching sourced sensory lead, so no description line sits alone as an orphan under the centred list; also state the pour size on spirits and say whether Brut Rosé is by the glass or the bottle once the draft or inputs supply it (the designer must not guess).

Criterion 13: add venue-type wording backed by the draft, such as a Spanish kicker on the section heads (Cócteles / Destilados / Vino / Cerveza de Barril / Sidra, with the English kept as subtitles), because a Mexican cantina menu whose only Spanish is the wordmark and two tequila items reads as a generic bar.

Criteria 10 and 14 (layout note for the designer): the centred cocktail block, with each price hung after its name, pushes every name off the centre axis, while the flush-left lower tier uses a different logic; the Draft Beer column also has no subhead, so Czech Pilsner sits one line above Blanco Tequila and Malbec, and the three lower-tier rows do not share baselines.

Criterion 12: use one voice for all descriptions, either ingredient lists everywhere or short sensory phrases everywhere, and write the cocktail ingredients in guest shorthand as the draft descriptions do ('lime', not 'fresh lime juice').
